In this book, Michael Mauboussin draws on his experience in the investment industry, combined with insights from psychology and science, to analyze the key reasons behind poor decision-making. He identifies the flaws in our thinking habits and offers a practical, three-step approach to help readers avoid making “foolish” mistakes. Being wrong isn’t the problem—the real danger lies in believing you can’t be wrong. If you don’t want your intelligence to backfire, it’s time to examine your mental blind spots and learn to “think again” before making important decisions. Let Columbia Business School’s “Professor of the Year,” Michael Mauboussin, guide you through a practical framework for training high-quality decision-making—so you can avoid costly errors and make smarter choices in life and work
